claims.text: The baseline Mo-Nb-Ta-W alloy is a single-phase disordered solid solution.
Adding less than 1 at.% Ti followed by controlled heat treatment will induce in situ Laves-phase precipitation.
The Ti-induced Laves precipitates will be coherent and nanoscale.
Trace Ti alters precipitate nucleation kinetics during heat treatment.
Coherent Laves precipitates impede elevated-temperature dislocation motion by acting as pinning sites.
At 900–1100°C, the Ti-modified alloy will have at least 20% higher yield strength than the Ti-free baseline.
At 900–1100°C under sustained loading, the Ti-modified alloy will have at least 20% better creep resistance than the Ti-free baseline.
Trace Ti addition and the resulting precipitates will not increase alloy density.
The modified alloy will retain room-temperature ductility and toughness comparable to the baseline.
The low density and controlled volume fraction of the precipitates prevent degradation of room-temperature ductility and toughness.
The expected benefit is limited to trace Ti contents below approximately 1 at.% and heat treatments that produce the desired coherent Laves phase.
Excess Ti or improper heat treatment could cause excessive precipitation or brittle-phase formation.
Excess Ti could significantly increase the alloy density.
Sustained loading and creep testing at 900–1100°C represent conditions typical of jet-turbine applications.
Prior studies on similar alloy systems suggest that minor Ti additions can trigger beneficial precipitation.
The optimal Ti concentration and heat-treatment parameters have not yet been determined.
